findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` requires the caller to satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`. A normal team admin is not a team owner, so the computed value is false and the mutation returns FORBIDDEN even though the UI and variable name treat team admins as allowed. Depending on whether `isTeamAdmin` also returns true for owners, owners may fail as well. This should use OR semantics, or a helper that checks either role.

findings.title: Guest filtering is case-sensitive and does not dedupe requests
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not, so a blacklisted address such as `evil@example.com` can be bypassed as `Evil@Example.com`. Existing-attendee checks are also case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), so mixed-case duplicates can be inserted. The request schema allows duplicate emails and the handler only compares each guest to existing attendees, not to other guests in the same request, so `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` creates duplicate Attendee rows and can send duplicate invitations. Normalize/lowercase addresses and dedupe both against existing attendees and within the request.

findings.title: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests
findings.body: The authorization check explicitly permits `isAttendee` callers to add guests. An external invitee who knows or guesses the numeric booking id can therefore append arbitrary email addresses, cause calendar invites to be sent, and trigger emails to all attendees that contain meeting details. Unless the product intentionally allows guests to invite further guests, this should be restricted to the organizer and authorized team admins/owners.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: The EventManager is constructed from `ctx.user` credentials. When the caller is a team admin/owner or attendee rather than the booking organizer, the calendar update runs with the wrong account and may fail or modify the organizer's calendar event under a different user's credentials. The handler already loads `booking.user` with credentials, so the organizer's credentials should be used for the booking's calendar update.

findings.title: Guests are persisted before the external calendar update
findings.body: `prisma.booking.update` inserts the new attendees before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs. If the calendar update throws, the API returns an error but the guest rows remain in the database. The user sees failure and retries, but the retry then reports `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests already exist. This leaves the operation in an ambiguous state; calendar sync failures should be handled without committing an unreported partial update.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the original guests list instead of the filtered list
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw request array, not `uniqueGuests`. If a request contains both an already-existing attendee and a new guest, the existing attendee is treated as newly added by the email manager and receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification. The email manager should receive only the guests that were actually inserted (`uniqueGuests`).

findings.title: addGuests emails ignore event type standard-email settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata`, unlike the surrounding `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendCancelledEmails`, etc. As a result, event types configured with `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` will still notify those users when guests are added. The handler has the event type and should pass metadata through so these settings are honored.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: The new endpoint has no tests covering authorization (organizer, team admin/owner, attendee), duplicate or mixed-case email handling, blacklist filtering, or email recipient selection. These are exactly the areas where the current implementation has defects, so endpoint-level tests would both catch regressions and document the intended permissions.
